source.title: A Diversity Diet for a Healthier Model: A Case Study of French ModernBERT
source.authors: Louis Estève; Christophe Servan; Thomas Lavergne; Agata Savary

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites scaling laws as background but does not test their loss-versus-scale relationships, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, or fit dependence. Its experiments vary pretraining data selection and evaluate downstream tasks.
record.gate_note: The reported pretraining loss curves are training-loss curves, not held-out cross-entropy measurements. The study uses one 200-million-parameter model size and a fixed compute budget for most runs; it does not fit scaling laws, test extrapolation, or compare compute-optimal parameter/token splits. The downstream benchmarks compare data-selection settings, not predictability from model scale or pretraining loss.
record.test_reason: Kaplan et al. is cited only as background. All encoders share one size (200M parameters), and most share one compute budget (483 H100 hours). The paper fits no scaling curve and reports no held-out loss. Its loss figure shows training loss across data-selection settings. Downstream scores compare sampling methods at fixed compute, not predictability from scale or loss.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that random and diversity-driven sampling can cut pretraining data by up to 94% and time by up to 73% while keeping performance. Diverse data also improves head-only fine-tuning on MEDIA and MultiATIS++.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies French ModernBERT data selection, not the scaling-law measurement or fitting procedures in the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Pretraining loss profiles differ between RANDOM and DIVERSE data; the authors report higher loss for DIVERSE encoders than their RANDOM counterparts. Dataset size is also reported to affect loss within each sampling type.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed model size and compute (483 H100 h), training on 105M to 401M words gives downstream fine-tuned scores comparable to a 2,379M-word topline trained for 1,775 h (Table 3). Diverse samples raise frozen-encoder scores by up to about 10 points (Table 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data diversity and selection can substitute for raw dataset size in encoder pretraining at fixed compute.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The loss curves are presented only as a figure, with no numerical loss values or uncertainty estimates; they are training loss rather than held-out loss. The study tests only one parameter count and does not fit scaling curves.
record.rows_left_out: Downstream benchmark tables were not extracted: they compare sampling datasets at a fixed model size and do not test downstream predictability from scale or pretraining loss. The table results are in Tables 3–4.

untested.parts: No held-out loss versus parameters, tokens or compute. There is a single model size and only training-loss curves.
No fits on small runs and no extrapolation.
No scaling-form test in other modalities or regimes.
Downstream scores vary with dataset size and sampling method at fixed compute. They are not related to scale or pretraining loss.

record.verdict_notes: The downstream tables (Tables 3–4) were rightly left out as rows: dataset size is confounded with epochs under fixed compute, and model size is constant. The paper measures no held-out loss.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute is measured.
No small-run fits or large-run loss predictions are tested.
No compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is measured.
No architecture variation at fixed parameter count is tested.
No scaling-law test in other modalities or training regimes is conducted.
Downstream tasks are evaluated across data-selection settings, but their predictability from scale or pretraining loss is not tested.
No scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal splits are fitted or compared across setups.

rows.subject: RANDOM-400M
rows.operation_detail: Pre-trained on randomly sampled data; smoothed training-loss profile reported.
rows.measure: Smoothed training loss over pre-training time
rows.note: The authors state that among RANDOM encoders, more data corresponds to higher loss. The plotted loss is training loss, not held-out loss.
rows.check: Training loss under fixed compute with repeated epochs. Higher loss with more data reflects less repetition, not held-out scaling. The 'observed' state has no version to refer to.

rows.note: The authors state that DIVERSE encoders have higher loss than their corresponding RANDOM encoders.
rows.check: Compares DIVERSE with RANDOM training loss, a data-composition effect. No scaling version applies.
